gap: No result ChatGPT got says how many hours of all-camera footage a card holds. Using Vantrue's 1 TB claims (as reported by The Weekly Driver), a 256 GB card holds about 9.5 h on the N4 Pro S with three cameras recording and about 10.2 h on the N5S with four. That is less than or barely one 10-hour rideshare shift, so a driver needs a 512 GB card (about 18.9 h / 20.5 h) to keep a full shift before loop recording overwrites it.
standout_why: I read Product Bible (cited in both chats), Dashlore (cited) and Redline Car Garage (cited). Product Bible gives only the largest card each camera takes and says 'Use a high-endurance card of at least 256GB for full shifts'. Dashlore gives the largest card size and VIOFO's BP60 parking-battery hours, with no recording hours per card. Redline gives card limits and no prices or hours. None of the three gives hours per card, bitrate or shifts per card, and Product Bible's advice that 256 GB covers a full shift doesn't hold for its own top pick by this arithmetic. ChatGPT repeated the '256GB or 512GB' advice to shoppers.
decides: The pick stays the same: the N4 Pro S and N5S are both ours, and the hours are close to a tie. The card advice changes: rideshare drivers on either camera should buy a 512 GB card or larger, not 256 GB. Vantrue's own N4 Pro S bundle (N4 Pro S + VP03 hardwire kit + 256GB card) comes with a card that holds about 9.5 h, under one 10-hour shift. Per GB, the N5S's fourth camera costs almost no recording time: 40 h against 37 h on 1 TB.
